subject: biology
title: Recombinant DNA and genetically modified organisms

scenes.heading: Recombinant DNA and GMOs
scenes.say: Before the nineteen eighties, people with type one diabetes used insulin from pigs and cattle. Today almost all insulin is made by bacteria or yeast carrying the human gene. Let's see how.
scenes.caption: Before the 1980s, people with type 1 diabetes used insulin from pigs and cattle. Today almost all insulin is made by bacteria or yeast carrying the human gene. Let's see how.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A USB stick carries a new app into a computer
scenes.science: A plasmid vector carries a gene of interest into a bacterium
scenes.breaks: a USB stick goes in every time, but only a small proportion of bacteria ever take up a plasmid, so selection is needed.
scenes.say: A plasmid is like a USB stick. It's a small circle of DNA that acts as a vector, carrying the gene of interest into a bacterium. The origin of replication lets it be copied, and a promoter lets the new gene run.

scenes.heading: Making recombinant bacteria
steps: Cut gene and plasmid: same enzyme
scenes.say: I Can Join To Select Gold. Isolate the gene, with no introns, because bacteria can't splice. Cut the gene and plasmid with the same restriction enzyme. Join them with ligase. Transform the bacteria using heat shock or electroporation. Then select the right ones and grow them.

scenes.heading: Selecting the right bacteria
points: Plasmid has ampR and tetR genes
Gene is inserted inside tetR, breaking it
Replica plating finds the missing colonies
scenes.say: Say the plasmid has genes for resistance to ampicillin and tetracycline, and the new gene is inserted inside the tetracycline gene, breaking it. Recombinant bacteria grow on ampicillin, but not on tetracycline. With replica plating, the colonies missing from the tetracycline plate are the ones you want.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: 50 colonies grow on ampicillin. Replica plated onto tetracycline, 35 grow. How many have the recombinant plasmid?
scenes.say: Fifty colonies grow on ampicillin, so all have a plasmid. Thirty-five also grow on tetracycline, so their plasmid has no insert. Fifty minus thirty-five gives fifteen recombinant colonies.
scenes.caption: 50 colonies grow on ampicillin, so all have a plasmid. 35 also grow on tetracycline, so their plasmid has no insert. 50 − 35 gives 15 recombinant colonies.

scenes.heading: GMO vs transgenic

left.title: GMO
points: e.g. CRISPR knockout of own gene

right.title: Transgenic
points: Has a gene from another species
e.g. Bt cotton, insulin E. coli

scenes.say: A GMO is any organism whose DNA has been changed by gene technology. A transgenic organism has a gene from a different species, like Bt cotton with a bacterial gene. Every transgenic organism is a GMO, but not every GMO is transgenic.

scenes.heading: Weighing it up
points: Genes may spread to wild relatives
scenes.say: GM crops like Bt cotton reduce insecticide spraying. But genes could spread to wild relatives, pests may evolve resistance, and patented seeds can be costly. For ethics questions, give a benefit and a concern.

points: Cut with the same enzyme, join with ligase
Transform, then select with marker genes
scenes.say: Quick recap. Cut the gene and plasmid with the same enzyme and join with ligase. Transform, then select using marker genes. And remember, transgenic means a gene from another species. Now try the practice questions!
